top_news.title: PhysMent: An Interactive Approach For LLM Reasoning In Physics Problems
top_news.dek: PhysMent is a new benchmark evaluating LLM physical reasoning through interactive, tool-mediated experimentation in a MuJoCo physics simulator.
top_news.brief: Unlike static benchmarks, PhysMent requires models to actively discover information by applying forces, querying object states, and modifying geometry. It tests the ability of LLMs to reason about the physical world through iterative interaction rather than just predicting static outcomes.
top_news.image_alt: A diagram showing an LLM interacting with a MuJoCo physics simulation environment.

top_news.title: [AINews] AEF-1 standard emerges for Third Party Evaluators, as Xai, OpenAI, and Anthropic all cosign
top_news.dek: Major AI labs including OpenAI, Anthropic, and xAI have co-signed the AEF-1 standard to formalize third-party evaluation of frontier models.
top_news.brief: The AEF-1 standard establishes a framework for embedded third-party evaluators, such as METR, to gain employee-like access to frontier AI companies. This initiative aims to verify safety practices, monitor incidents, and ensure adherence to pacing commitments as models advance.
top_news.image_alt: A conceptual graphic representing collaborative AI safety and evaluation standards.

top_news.title: Introducing Gemini 3.8 Live and 3.8 Live Extended Thinking
top_news.dek: Google has released Gemini 3.8 Live and Gemini 3.8 Live Extended Thinking, featuring improved parallel reasoning for complex voice-based tasks.
top_news.brief: The new models focus on enhanced dialogue capabilities and intelligence, specifically designed for intuitive collaboration. The Extended Thinking variant is optimized for executing multi-step tasks via voice input.
top_news.image_alt: Gemini 3.8 branding on a light blue background

top_news.title: Agility’s new humanoid robot will stop, squat to avoid harming human coworkers
top_news.dek: Agility Robotics introduced the Digit 5, a humanoid robot capable of operating safely alongside humans without physical barriers.
top_news.brief: The robot features safety mechanisms that allow it to stop or squat when detecting humans, enabling deployment in warehouses and factories without isolated work cells.

top_news.title: openarm: A fully open-source humanoid arm for physical AI research and deployment in contact-rich environments
top_news.dek: The OpenArm project provides a fully open-source humanoid arm design for physical AI research and contact-rich environment deployment.
top_news.brief: This hardware initiative aims to lower the barrier for researchers working on physical AI, providing an accessible platform for testing robotics in complex, real-world interactions.
